extracted.intended_audience: bacteriology laboratory students, technicians, and researchers performing experimental animal inoculation, toxin testing, and haemolysin work
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evaluative standards for preparing bacterial cultivations, performing serial dilutions, inoculating animals, testing toxins, raising/attenuating virulence, immunising animals, preparing and titrating haemolytic serum, and related animal-care and legal/ethical requirements in a bacteriological laboratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivation preparation (optimum medium, temperature, activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cultivation must be prepared on a solid medium of the optimum reaction, incubated at the optimum temperature, and injected at the period of greatest activity and vigour, of the particular organism it is desired to test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the correct solid medium and incubation conditions tailored to the organism; time inoculation to when the organism shows peak activity for reproducible infectivity results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serial dilutions using sterile capsules and pipettes
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare serial dilutions by emulsifying one loopful of growth in 10 c.c. bouillon (capsule I = 1 c.c. = 0.1 loop), then transferring 0.1 c.c. to 9.9 c.c. for successive ten-fold dilutions to obtain defined concentrations (e.g., capsule II 0.001 loop per c.c., III 0.00001, IV 0.0000001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sterile graduated pipettes, arrange labelled sterile capsules (I–IV), and follow the described transfer volumes precisely; summarize dilutions in a table and make up small-volume doses to standard volumes (1 c.c.) before inoculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict aseptic technique and contamination precautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe the usual precautions against contamination when removing loopfuls and transferring fluids; use sterile apparatus and dispose of infected instruments (e.g., drop infected pipette into lysol solution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain sterility of media, pipettes, syringes and capsules throughout; sterilize or safely discard contaminated implements as directed to prevent cross-contamination of dilutions and animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of multiples of the loop for dose variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiples of the loop are prepared by emulsifying 1, 2, 5, or 10 loops each with 1 c.c. sterile bouillon in separate sterile capsules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare these multiplicative doses in separate sterile vessels to create a defined range of inoculum sizes for comparative infectivity assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syringe filling and inoculation order
rubrics_metrics.description: Inoculate a series of animals filling the syringe first from that capsule containing the smallest dose, then from the capsule containing the next smallest, and so on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If care is taken, it will not be necessary to sterilise the syringe during the series of inoculations; begin with smallest dose to avoid carryover contamination of lower doses into later animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumeration of organisms from plated dilutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant tubes of gelatine or agar from each of the higher dilutions, pour plates and incubate. When growth is visible enumerate the number of organisms present in each, average up and calculate the number of bacteria present in one loopful of the inoculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appropriate dilution range (e.g., 0.0000001 to 0.01 loop), incubate under correct conditions, count colonies, average replicate plates, and perform quantitative calculations (use percentage formula if exactitude is essential).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal lethal dose (m.l.d.) determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The smallest dose which causes the infection and death of the inoculated animal is noted as the minimal lethal dose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and compare doses across species/individuals; use serial dilutions and repeated experiments to estimate m.l.d. reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of flask cultivations for toxin testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare flask cultivations of the organism under observation in glucose formate broth, and incubate for fourteen days under optimum conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified broth and incubate for the stated period to allow sufficient toxin production prior to separation/assay procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intracellular (insoluble) toxin testing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat the fluid culture in a water-bath at 60 deg. C. for thirty minutes (producing a sterile, turbid 'killed' culture); inoculate a control tube of bouillon to demonstrate freedom from living bacteria; inject intravenously that amount corresponding to 1 per cent. of the animal's body-weight; observe up to twenty-eight days and perform complete post-mortem on death; repeat experiment and estimate minimal lethal dose of 'killed' culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include sterility controls and repeat positive tests; use the same unit concept (1 c.c. of toxin) analogous to loopful units for living cultures when calculating m.l.d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extracellular (soluble) toxin testing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter the cultivation through a porcelain filter candle (Berkefeld) into a sterile filter flask; inoculate mice, rats, guinea-pigs, and rabbits subcutaneously with that quantity of toxin corresponding to 1 per cent. of body-weight; inoculate a 'control' tube of bouillon to confirm sterility; observe up to one month; perform complete post-mortem on fatalities; repeat and ascertain minimal lethal dose for each susceptible species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure filtration apparatus is correctly set up (see figure), include sterility controls, and use species-appropriate dosing and observation periods to determine toxicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Martin's small filter candle for small-volume filtrations
rubrics_metrics.description: When only a bouillon-tube culture is available, employ Martin's small filter candle and tube specially designed for filtration of small quantities to obtain a germ-free filtrate rapidly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble the narrow filter flask and tubular Chamberland candle as described, connect to an exhaust pump, and pour cultivation into funnel head to obtain sterile filtrate into test-tube receiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raising (exalting) virulence by passage
rubrics_metrics.description: Passage of virus: inoculate pure cultivations into highly susceptible animals and pass rapidly from animal to animal, selecting the method of inoculation that places the organism under most favorable conditions for growth and multiplication (e.g., intraperitoneal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use serial passage through susceptible hosts to select for higher virulence; choose inoculation route that maximizes organism growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raising virulence by co-inoculation with virulent organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Virus plus virulent organisms: inoculate the organism together with pure cultivations of some other microbe sufficiently virulent to ensure death of the experimental animal; the association may increase the virulence of the low-virulence organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-inoculation can accelerate selection for virulence; follow with passages if increased virulence is observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raising virulence by co-injection with toxins
rubrics_metrics.description: Virus plus toxins: inoculate the organism together with subcutaneous, intraperitoneal, or intravenous injection of a toxin to lower the host's natural resistance and enable the organism to multiply and subsequently be exalted in virulence by passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of toxin relative to organism (simultaneous, before, or immediately after) may vary; use toxins known to lower resistance (e.g., proteus group toxins).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attenuation (lowering) of virulence methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Attenuation is usually effected by varying the environment of the cultivations: (1) cultivating in unsuitable media by composition or reaction; (2) at unsuitable temperature; (3) in unsuitable atmosphere; (4) under unfavorable conditions as to light, motion, etc.; and also by (5) passage through naturally resistant animals; (6) exposure to desiccation; (7) exposure to gaseous disinfectants; (8) combination of methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select attenuation method(s) appropriate to the organism and purpose; combinations often increase attenuation effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of immunisation (active and combined)
rubrics_metrics.description: Active immunisation methods include (I) inoculation with dead bacteria (killed by heat, UV, chemical germicides, or autolysis), (II) inoculation of attenuated strains, (III) inoculation of living virulent bacteria; combined active and passive immunisation includes (IV) inoculation of toxin-antitoxin mixtures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose immunisation strategy appropriate to the antibody required (e.g., dead cultures for safe antibody production versus live strains for full immunity); combinations may be necessary for particular cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rabbit immunisation protocol and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a full-grown rabbit (1200–1500 g, preferably 2000 g+), observe weight and temperature; follow a schedule of inoculations with killed cultivation (e.g., 2 c.c. IV and 10 c.c. intraperitoneal initial, then escalating killed doses and subsequent injections of live minimal lethal doses subcutaneously and intraperitoneally), regulate by animal's condition, increase living doses by multiples of ten, and collect blood at intervals to test serum for specific antibodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test killed cultures for sterility (incubation of transferred broth), determine minimal lethal dose of live strain on mice beforehand, allow recovery periods (~7 days) and monitor weight/temperature charts; immunity indicated by tolerance to large doses and protective activity of serum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibody formation without completing full immunisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific antibody is always formed in greater or lesser amount provided death does not immediately follow the antigen injection; for some purposes, sufficient antibody (e.g., agglutinin or haemolysin) can be obtained without carrying immunisation to full immunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stop immunisation when desired antibody titer is reached; use serum assays to decide when to halt inoculations if full immunity is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complement and haemolysin principles (inactivation/reactivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complement (alexine) is thermo-labile and present in normal serum; haemolysin (immune body) is thermostable antibody. Haemolysin is obtained by exposing immune serum to 56 deg. C for 15–30 minutes to destroy complement (inactivated), and is reactivated by addition of fresh normal serum containing complement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use heating steps to separate complement and haemolysin for haemolytic assays; guinea-pig serum commonly used as complement source; take care with temperatures and times to avoid loss of haemolytic power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of haemolytic serum (rabbit immunisation with washed human erythrocytes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select healthy rabbit (≥2500 g), inject intraperitoneally with washed human red cells in staged doses (e.g., 2 c.c. citrated blood centrifuged and washed, followed by injections at 7-day intervals of increasing cell volumes mixed with saline), and after series collect blood, separate serum and inactivate by heating at 56 deg. C for 15 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wash erythrocytes thoroughly, maintain aseptic technique, prefer intravenous route for later injections for better results but take care to avoid air embolism, and test preliminary serum samples to assess haemolytic activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titration of haemolytic serum and definition of minimal haemolytic dose (M.H.D.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform serial dilutions of inactivated haemolytic serum, add erythrocyte solution, incubate, then add complement and incubate; examine tubes for complete haemolysis (clear red solution) versus absence (deposit of red cells). The smallest amount causing complete haemolysis is the minimal haemolytic dose (M.H.D.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up dilution series carefully (as given), use fresh complement (guinea-pig serum), incubate at 37 deg. C for specified times, and interpret haemolysis; a serum giving complete haemolysis down to tube 7 (M.H.D. .005 c.c.) is strong (~200 M.H.D. per c.c.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage of haemolysin (ampouling, inactivation, refrigeration)
rubrics_metrics.description: When haemolysin content is sufficient, kill the rabbit, collect blood aseptically, centrifuge, pipette clear serum into 1 c.c. glass ampoules, hermetically seal, heat ampoules in water-bath at 56 deg. C for 30 minutes to destroy complement and ensure sterility, and store ampoules in a closed metal box in the ice chest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overheating (longer exposure reduces haemolytic power); ensure aseptic collection, proper sealing, correct heat inactivation timing, and cold storage for long-term preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental planning, animal welfare and legal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan experiments to secure maximum information and minimum discomfort; ensure virus is introduced into the exact tissue or organ selected; operation must be done with skill, expedition, and under strictly aseptic conditions. In some countries experiments on animals require government license and certificates (e.g., Home Secretary license in England) with stipulations such as destruction of animal if it shows pain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain required licenses/certificates for procedures (Certificate A for simple hypodermic inoculations and venesections, Certificate B for procedures allowing survival beyond anaesthesia, and additional certificates for certain species); adhere to legal and ethical obligations including immediate destruction if animal shows pain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-inoculation examination and record-keeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Before inoculation examine animals to avoid using diseased subjects: observe at rest and in motion, inspect fur/feathers/scales, eyes and external orifices, palpate groins and abdomen, note sex, weight, rectal temperature, time of inoculation, material, method and authority; enter data on an inoculation card with space for course notes and weight/temperature charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform microscopic examination of blood films when indicated, record baseline metrics and subsequent observations on standardized cards (e.g., pink inoculation card) for reproducibility and welfare monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening for and treating common natural infections in laboratory animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize common infections by species (e.g., rabbit Psoric Acari causing mange; mouse/rat septicaemia and coccidia; guinea pig tuberculosis; monkey tuberculosis). If saving infected animals: segregate, clean scabs, treat with 5% potassium persulphate or paraffin/vaseline with lysol drops, disinfect cages and inspect neighbours; test certain animals with Old Tuberculin on arrival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segregate infected animals, perform topical and environmental treatments, inspect and treat contacts, and use diagnostic tests (e.g., Koch's Old Tuberculin) for tuberculosis screening in susceptible species.
